title: New Hire Impact Pathways and Manager Templates
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines an "impact-first" approach to new-hire integration at Redwood Inference. It combines a hiring intake checklist, a manager-driven onboarding curriculum, and concrete evaluation templates that emphasize early, measurable contribution while preserving psychological safety and learning. The goal is to shorten time-to-impact without sacrificing long-term retention or technical correctness.

When to use this document:
- For managers hiring ICs or managers for new or expanding roles.
- For people-ops partners designing role activation gates.
- For hiring panels that need a calibrated readiness rubric.

Key principles:
- Task-first learning: New hires demonstrate value through small, scoped deliverables (not just shadowing).
- Role activation gates: Clear, binary checkpoints at 30/60/90 days with observable evidence.
- Manager enablement: Managers receive templates and cadence guidance to run a predictable integration.
- Cross-functional alignment: Early stakeholder mapping to remove blockers.

1) Hiring intake and role definition (before offer)

Objective: Ensure each hire has a concrete first-90-day success plan embedded in the job description and interview process.

Checklist (hiring manager + people-ops):
1. Define three concrete impact deliverables for 90 days (examples: implement a lightweight telemetry hook for a model endpoint, complete onboarding cert for infra repo, ship a doc describing a cross-team integration).
2. Create a candidate assessment matrix (skills, culture add, ramp potential) with weightings (example below).
3. Identify onboarding sponsor (peer-level buddy) and 30/60/90 owner (usually the manager).
4. Allocate budget for dedicated onboarding time in calendar (2 hours/day for the first two weeks).
5. Pre-provision accounts and request access list to SSO, relevant repos, Slack channels, cloud tenants.

Sample candidate assessment matrix (weights):
- Core role skills: 45%
- System/product understanding: 20%
- Collaboration & communication: 15%
- Learning velocity / problem-solving: 10%
- Cultural fit & values: 10%

Interview guidance: Every stage should include one exercise tied to an actual 90-day deliverable. For ICs this might be a design sketch or small code review; for PMs, a prioritization memo. Hiring panels should record evidence against the assessment matrix.

2) Preboarding (offer -> first day)

Owner: people-ops + hiring manager
Timeline: offer signed -> day 0 (start)

Actions:
- Send a 7-day preboarding packet with a short "first-week goals" one-pager.
- Share an intro to the team's 90-day deliverables and the onboarding mentor.
- Ensure these accesses are provisioned 48–72 hours before start:

Access provisioning table:
| Access | Owner | Required by | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SSO (Okta) | IT Ops | 72h | Assign to primary group for team resources |
| GitHub team | Repo owner | 48h | Add to infra and service repos with write where needed |
| Cloud project | Cloud infra | 72h | Minimal privileges; escalate to infra for elevated tasks |
| Internal wiki / Confluence | People Ops | 48h | Grant edit rights to onboarding docs |
| Slack channels | Hiring manager | 24h | Add to #team, #oncall if applicable |

3) First-week plan (days 0–7):

Goals: reduce friction, build context, deliver first tiny win.

Day-by-day checklist for manager:
- Day 0: Welcome + orientation (1 hour), passkeys/KMS intro, calendar walkthrough, logistics.
- Day 1: Team kickoff + product context (2 hours), assign first tiny win (example: reproduce a perf benchmark).
- Day 2–3: Dev environment provisioning workshop with buddy (pairing session).
- Day 4: Small scoped PR or doc assigned and merged (first tiny win).
- Day 5: First-week retrospective with manager (30 min) — surface blockers and learning plan.

Manager templates (copy/paste):
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — Week 0 Plan and Resources"
- Welcome email body (short):
"Hi [Name], welcome to the team! Attached is your Week 0 playbook: setup steps, access links, and an initial tiny win to get you moving. Your buddy is [Buddy Name]. I’ll check in daily for the first two weeks. Looking forward to working together — Maya"

4) 30/60/90 day activation gates (observable evidence required)

Structure: For each gate, managers collect 3 artifacts that demonstrate readiness. Artifacts are one of: merged PR, architecture note, stakeholder sign-off, production telemetry, or recorded demo.

30-day gate (onboarding-enabled):
- Evidence examples: dev environment reliably working; merged tiny-win PR; completed onboarding checklist.
- Pass criteria: can perform core dev workflows with <2 escalations/week; demonstrates basic code / docs standards.

60-day gate (contributing independently):
- Evidence examples: shipped a small feature or bugfix end-to-end assigned by manager; led one team sync; documented a cross-team integration requirement.
- Pass criteria: owns at least one backlog item from design to deploy with manager oversight; provides clear, timely status updates.

90-day gate (impact and ownership):
- Evidence examples: primary owner of a deliverable that impacts customers or internal metrics; presented runbook or postmortem; measurable improvement in a metric (e.g., latency, test coverage).
- Pass criteria: operating independently on scoped work, receiving positive peer feedback, and able to onboard a new hire to a portion of their work.

5) Manager toolkit: recurring cadences and artifacts

Required cadences (minimum):
- Daily quick sync (first 14 days): 10–15 min
- Weekly 1:1: structured agenda (see template)
- 30/60/90 gate reviews (30–60 min each): manager + buddy + people-ops as needed

Weekly 1:1 template (30 min):
1. Quick status (3 min): wins / blockers
2. Focus for the week (10 min): align on work and priorities
3. Growth & feedback (10 min): pair coaching, knowledge gaps
4. Admin & actions (7 min): access issues, calendar, upcoming milestones

One-page performance rubric for first 90 days (use for calibration):
- Contribution velocity: Exceeds / Meets / Below expectations (evidence: number of merged items, size & impact)
- Code quality & review behavior: Exceeds / Meets / Below (evidence: review comments, test coverage)
- Cross-team collaboration: Exceeds / Meets / Below (evidence: stakeholder sign-offs)
- Learning & autonomy: Exceeds / Meets / Below (evidence: time-to-triage, ramp of new tech)

6) Feedback and calibration process

- Managers submit a short "90-day readiness memo" to people-ops when the new hire reaches 90 days. The memo is a 3-paragraph summary: context, evidence (3 artifacts), and recommendation (pass, extend mentoring, role change).
- Quarterly calibration: hiring managers meet in a 60-minute forum each quarter to review a sample of readiness memos for consistency. People-ops provides a calibration sheet (spreadsheet) with anonymized evidence to reduce bias.

Template: 90-day readiness memo (subject + body)
Subject: "90-day readiness: [Name] — [Role]"
Body:
"Context: brief 2–3 lines about role and initial deliverable scope.
Evidence: bullet list of artifacts with links (PRs, docs, demo recordings).
Recommendation: Pass / Extend (30 days) / Role adjustment. Rationale: 2–3 lines."

7) Manager escalation and extension protocol

If a hire does not meet pass criteria at a gate, follow this protocol:
1. Manager documents gaps and proposes an extension plan (30 days) with explicit milestones.
2. People-ops reviews and approves extension parameters and resources (e.g., extra mentor time).
3. At extension conclusion, repeat gate review with the same artifact requirements.
4. If gaps persist, org HR escalation is triggered for performance improvement planning (PIP) per HR policy.

8) Templates and snippets (copy-paste)

Manager weekly status request to stakeholder group:
"Hi team — quick FYI: [New Hire Name] is onboarding this sprint and will be owning [deliverable]. We may request quick reviews on [date]. If you have constraints, please let [Manager] know"

Peer feedback prompt (to request structured feedback):
"Please share 3 short observations about [Name] from your interactions: 1) what they did well, 2) one thing to improve, 3) readiness rating (1–5)."

9) Measuring success (KPIs for the program)

Primary metrics (people-ops + manager tracked):
- Time-to-independent-contributor (median days to pass 90-day gate)
- New-hire attrition at 6 months
- Manager satisfaction with onboarding (pulse survey score)
- Fraction of hires passing 90-day gate without extension

Data sources: HRIS, GitHub activity, Confluence artifact links, onboarding surveys. People-ops will publish quarterly dashboards.

10) Related tools and automation suggestions

- Automate access provisioning with a prefilled Jira form triggered on offer acceptance.
- Template the 30/60/90 gate as a checklist in Confluence with required artifact link fields.
- Slack shortcut to request first-week pairing sessions with buddy.

Appendix A — Example first tiny-win assignments by role
- Backend engineer: add metrics to an existing model-serving endpoint and create a dashboard tile.
- Research engineer: run a standard eval harness on a new model variant and summarize results.
- Product manager: scope and write acceptance criteria for a telemetry feature and align stakeholders.
- Support engineer: create troubleshooting runbook for the top two customer issues.

Appendix B — Example evaluation artifacts (what counts)
- Merged PR with passing CI and reviewer sign-off
- Design doc less than 2 pages with peer feedback incorporated
- Recorded 10-minute demo showing feature and tests
- Stakeholder email confirming extract of requirements
